library.author: Mikhail Lermontov
library.section: Part Two, Princess Mary — journal entry «Вот уже полтора месяца...
library.translation: I have long been living not with my heart but with my head. I weigh and analyse my own passions and actions with strict curiosity, but without involvement. (my translation)
library.quote: Я давно уж живу не сердцем, а головою. / Я взвешиваю, разбираю свои собственные страсти и поступки с строгим любопытством, но без участия.
library.thought: Pechorin is the guy by the booth with his arms crossed, watching himself dance. He isn't bragging; he sounds tired. 'Strict curiosity, but without involvement' is the most honest description of a bad night out I've read.

track.title: Pain in the Ass
track.note: Detached, deadpan deep house with a half-spoken vocal: the head is in the room but the heart isn't, just like Pechorin.

library.author: Hyun Jin-geon
library.section: The ending (Kim Cheomji returns home with the seolleongtang)
library.translation: "I bought you seolleongtang, why can't you eat it, why can't you eat it... how strange, today! And my luck was so good..." (my translation)
library.quote: 설렁탕을 사다놓았는데 왜 먹지를 못하니, 왜 먹지를 못하니... 괴상하게도 오늘은! 운수가 좋더니만...
library.thought: All day the rickshaw man kept winning fares and kept stalling his way home, drinking because the luck felt too good to be safe. The soup he promised arrives and his wife is gone. The repetition is the whole tragedy — he keeps saying the same thing as if the loop could change the ending.

track.title: It Makes You Forget (Itgehane)
track.note: A bright, looping Korean-titled house tune about forgetting — exactly what Kim Cheomji tries to do in the tavern, and exactly what the last page won't let him.

library.author: Lu Xun
library.section: Section 10 (the madman confronts his elder brother); the line recurs in sections 3 and 10
library.translation: 'It has always been like this — does that make it right?' (my translation)
library.quote: 『從來如此，便對麽？』
library.thought: Four characters of tradition and then the one question nobody on the village road will answer. Lu Xun puts it in the mouth of the man everyone calls mad, which is the joke and the knife. Under a strobe it reads like a heckle at the whole room: we dance like this because we always have — fine, but is it right?

track.title: King of Hosts
track.note: Tzusing's paranoid, clanking industrial pulse sounds like the madman's village closing in — hosts who smile with their teeth.

library.author: Yordan Yovkov
library.section: Act One, opening stage direction (the steam mill)
library.translation: From inside, at the far end of the mill, comes the unbroken noise of the millstones and the steady beats of the smoke in the iron chimney. (my translation)
library.quote: Навътре, към другия край на мелницата, непрекъснато се чува шумът на мелничните камъни и равномерните удари на дима в железния комин.
library.thought: Yovkov scores his village tragedy with a machine: millstones grinding, smoke pulsing 'evenly' in the chimney. It's literally a four-on-the-floor under every scene of desire and gossip. The mill is the club, and Albena is the one everyone is watching from the bench.

track.title: Metropole
track.note: A steady, mechanical deep groove to sit under the endless thud of the mill's chimney.

library.author: Lewis Carroll
library.section: Chapter VI, "Pig and Pepper" (Alice meets the Cheshire Cat)
library.quote: Oh, you can’t help that,” said the Cat: “we’re all mad here. I’m mad. You’re mad.
library.thought: The Cat doesn’t argue, it just includes you. That’s basically the door policy here: once you’re through, you’re already part of the madness. Alice wants a logical exit and the Cat offers belonging instead.

track.title: Hyph Mngo
track.note: Giddy, pitched-up and slightly unhinged in the friendliest way, like a grin hanging in the dark after the rest of the room has vanished.

library.author: Elin Pelin
library.section: Opening dialogue between the cart driver and the court official
library.translation: "You write them off, sir, we don't know how to write," said the lad. (my translation)
library.quote: — Пиши ги ти, господине, ние не знаем да пишем — рече момъкът
library.thought: The official sneers that peasants should be 'written off as a lost people', and Andreshko turns the verb right back at him. One line, and literacy becomes power and power becomes a joke. Every bouncer-and-guestlist argument I've ever overheard has this exact shape.

track.title: Bad Kingdom
track.note: A brooding song about who rules and who gets ruled, for a boy outwitting the man with the papers on a muddy road.

library.author: Kim Sowol
library.section: Stanza 3 (modern Korean text)
library.translation: With each step as you go, / tread softly, pressing down / on the flowers laid before you. (my translation)
library.quote: 가시는 걸음 걸음 / 놓인 그 꽃을 / 사뿐히 즈려밟고 가시옵소서.
library.thought: She scatters azaleas from Yaksan on the road of the one leaving her and asks him to step on them gently — devotion and accusation in the same gesture. 'Sappunhi' is a dancer's word, light-footed. Every exit from a dancefloor should feel this tender and this crushed.

track.title: Raingurl
track.note: Yaeji's soft-spoken Korean-American house is both gentle and stubborn, the same way Sowol's speaker refuses to cry while laying flowers under the departing feet.

library.author: Rubén Darío
library.section: 'El rey burgués (canto alegre)', first paragraph
library.translation: Was he a poet king? No, my friend: he was the Bourgeois King. (my translation)
library.quote: ¿Era un rey poeta? No, amigo mío: era el Rey Burgués.
library.thought: Darío builds a king out of pure luxury — horses, gold, fanfares — and then deflates him in one line. It's the VIP-section problem: everything money can buy except the thing that makes it sing. The poet in this story ends up freezing outside cranking a barrel organ.

track.title: Colibria
track.note: Andean flutes and hand percussion over a slow pulse — the music of the street poet, not the gilded court.

library.author: Aleko Konstantinov
library.section: Бай Ганьо тръгна по Европа": the opening frame ("Начало") and the first paragraphs of chapter I, "Бай Ганьо пътува" (Bay Ganyo Travels), at the Pest railway station buffet
library.translation: "Absorbed in the noise, I didn't notice when Bay Ganyo slipped out of the restaurant with his saddlebags. Where's Bay Ganyo? His glass is empty." (my translation)
library.quote: Залисан в шума, не забележих кога бай Ганьо изфирясал от ресторана заедно с дисагите си. Де бай Ганя? Чашата му празна.
library.thought: The book opens by telling us that Bay Ganyo swapped his Ottoman cloak for a Belgian mantle and everyone decided he was "a full European". The first scene shows how thin that coat is. He's in a grand station buffet in Pest, and the first thing he does is disappear, saddlebags and all, leaving an empty glass. The narrator has to search the whole platform for him. I like that Konstantinov frames the book as friends talking over each other ("No, me, you don't know anything!") to tell Bay Ganyo stories. The satire is told as gossip, so the reader is pulled into the laughing, and the laugh is never fully at someone else's expense. The prose is quick, colloquial and full of Turkish-flavoured words like "изфирясал" and "дисаги". It's a rogue's road trip, and it reads like 1895 stand-up.

track.title: Perth
track.note: Restless, jacking Sofia hardware house for Bay Ganyo, who can't sit still at the buffet.

library.author: Natsume Sōseki
library.section: Chapter 1, opening paragraph
library.translation: Thanks to the recklessness I inherited from my parents, I've been losing out ever since I was a kid. Once in primary school I jumped from the second floor of the school building and couldn't stand up properly for a week. (my translation)
library.quote: 親譲りの無鉄砲で小供の時から損ばかりしている。 / 小学校に居る時分学校の二階から飛び降りて一週間ほど腰を抜かした事がある。
library.thought: Every rave has one of these: the person who climbs the speaker stack because someone said they wouldn't dare. Sōseki makes the injury sound like a badge, and the narrator files 'losing out' as a family heirloom rather than a regret. I read this at 2am and thought of everyone I've watched land badly and grin about it.

track.title: Sumo Jungle
track.note: Terada's breakneck, cheeky jungle has the same headlong, slightly ridiculous momentum as a boy leaping out of a second-floor window on a dare.

library.author: Li Bai
library.section: Lines 5–6 (the turn from the Yellow River and white hair to the feast)
library.translation: When life goes your way, take your joy to the full; never let the golden cup face the moon empty. (my translation)
library.quote: 人生得意須盡歡，莫使金樽空對月。
library.thought: The poem opens on the river that never flows back and hair gone white by evening, and only then says: drink. The joy is an argument against the clock, not a forgetting of it. The empty cup facing the moon is the loneliest image here — the moon showed up, so should you.

track.title: They Drink
track.note: Gooooose's woozy, sparkling electronics from the Shanghai underground feel like Li Bai's third-hundredth cup raised to the moon.

library.author: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu
library.section: Chapter I, "An Early Fright". It runs from the opening ("In Styria, we, though by no means magnificent people, inhabit a castle...") to the end of the chapter (the priest's prayer in the nursery).
library.quote: I was wakened by a sensation as if two needles ran into my breast very deep at the same moment, and I cried loudly.
library.thought: The horror arrives right after comfort. The strange lady caresses six-year-old Laura, lies down beside her, and soothes her back to sleep, and only then come the "two needles." The scene that frightened me more, though, is what happens next. Laura tells us she was "studiously kept in ignorance of ghost stories," which was meant to protect her. Instead it leaves her with no words for what happened, and the adults don't give her any. Her father laughs and calls it a dream. The nursery maid claims it was her face Laura saw. Meanwhile the housekeeper whispers that "the place is still warm," and they keep a servant sitting up in the nursery for eight years. Everyone in the house acts like they believe her while telling her not to. The real gothic engine here is a household protecting a child by lying to her, and the novel is built on that.

track.title: The Host of Seraphim (Foxtrot rave edit)
track.note: Cathedral vocals over a slow, heavy techno pulse for Carmilla's haunted nursery.

library.author: Miguel de Cervantes
library.original: El ingenioso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha
library.section: Part I, Chapter I, opening
library.translation: In a village of La Mancha, whose name I do not care to remember, there lived not long ago a gentleman of the lance-on-the-rack kind, with an old shield, a skinny nag and a racing greyhound. (my translation)
library.quote: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, no ha mucho / tiempo que vivía un hidalgo de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, / rocín flaco y galgo corredor.
library.thought: The most famous opening in Spanish starts by refusing to tell you where you are — like a party location that's only texted an hour before. And the inventory is all faded gear: an old shield, a skinny horse. Nobody here is a hero yet; that's the joke and the tenderness.

track.title: Destiny
track.note: A sunlit, slightly wistful Barcelona house track for a man about to talk himself into a destiny out of old equipment and a bony horse.

library.author: Cao Xueqin
library.section: Chapter 1 (第一回), the couplet on the gate of the Illusory Land of Great Void in Zhen Shiyin's dream
library.translation: When the false is taken for true, the true becomes false; where nothing is taken for something, something turns to nothing. (my translation)
library.quote: 假作真時真亦假，無為有處有還無。
library.thought: Zhen Shiyin dozes off over a book on a hot afternoon and walks up to a stone arch carrying this couplet — the whole novel's warning, hung over a doorway. At 4am it's the realest line I know: the fog machine, the faces, the feeling that this is more true than the daylight. The book says pass through the gate anyway.

track.title: The Gate
track.note: The opener of Mù Chè Shān Chū is literally a threshold track — slow, misty Chinese timbres for stepping under Cao Xueqin's arch into the dream.

library.author: Ivan Turgenev
library.section: Chapter IX
library.translation: and I sat, looked, listened, and filled up entirely with some nameless feeling that held everything: sadness and joy, a premonition of the future, desire, and the fear of life. (my translation)
library.quote: а я сидел, глядел, слушал и наполнялся весь каким-то безыменным ощущением, в котором было всё: и грусть, и радость, и предчувствие будущего, и желание, и страх жизни.
library.thought: Sixteen, legs hanging off a broken greenhouse wall, and he feels everything at once without a name for any of it. Then the last line of the paragraph gives it one name anyway: Zinaida. That's the chill-out room at sunrise, crushing on someone you met three hours ago.

track.title: Ariadna
track.note: Dreamy Moscow synth-pop with a woman's name in the title, as hazy and wordless as the feeling Vladimir can only call Zinaida.

library.author: Mary Shelley
library.section: Volume III, Chapter 20 (the creature confronts Victor after he destroys the unfinished mate)
library.quote: Remember that I have power; you believe yourself miserable, but I can make you so wretched that the light of day will be hateful to you. / You are my creator, but I am your master;
library.thought: The whole power balance flips in one semicolon: the made thing now gives orders to the maker. Standing under a rig of machines we built to move us, it lands a little too close. Victor wanted to play god for a night and got the comedown forever.

track.title: Firestarter
track.note: A snarling, self-proclaimed menace over broken beats: the creature finally talking back to his creator in a voice nobody can ignore.

library.author: Hristo Botev
library.section: The whole ballad, all 12 stanzas, from "Жив е той, жив е! Там на Балкана" to "и слънцето пак пече ли - пече!
library.translation: He who falls in battle for freedom / does not die: he is mourned / by earth and sky, beast and nature (my translation)
library.quote: Тоз, който падне в бой за свобода, / той не умира: него жалеят / земя и небо, звяр и природа
library.thought: The poem is built like a single day turning into night and back into day. It opens in harsh noon heat, with a harvest girl singing while the hero bleeds. Night brings the eagle, the gentle wolf, the samodivi (forest spirits) and the mountain singing an outlaw song. Then dawn puts us right back where we started: the same wound, the same blood, "and the sun keeps burning, burning." What gets me is that the consolation in the middle never cancels the brutality on either side of it. Botev hands you the myth of immortality and then makes you look at the real sun again. Even the repetition at the end, "пече ли - пече," has a looping pulse, like a beat that won't drop out.

track.title: Cloud Generator
track.note: A slow climb into a euphoric lift, like Botev's turn from bleeding noon to the night when the Balkan mountain sings.

library.author: Dante Alighieri
library.section: Canto I, lines 1–3
library.translation: Midway along the road of our life I found myself in a dark wood, for the straight way was lost. (my translation)
library.quote: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita / mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, / ché la diritta via era smarrita.
library.thought: 'Mi ritrovai' — I found myself — not 'I went'. Nobody decides to get lost in the dark wood, you just look up at 3 a.m. and the exit signs are gone. Dante makes it 'our' life in line one, so the whole crowd is lost together.

track.title: Another Earth
track.note: Brooding, cinematic Italian melodic techno for the descent into the dark wood.

library.author: Walt Whitman
library.section: Song of Myself", sections 1–3 (from "I celebrate myself, and sing myself," through "Till that becomes unseen and receives proof in its turn.")
library.quote: There was never any more inception than there is now, / Nor any more youth or age than there is now, / And will never be any more perfection than there is now, / Nor any more heaven or hell than there is now.
library.thought: Section 2 tells the reader to stop taking things "at second or third hand" and to stop feeding "on the spectres in books." Whitman puts that in a book, and a few lines later he adds "You shall not look through my eyes either." I find that reading has more to it than fetching text and pulling out a quote. Section 3 says the beginning is happening now, not in some origin story. The beginning is this breath, the bass in the floor, the line I'm reading. A rave works the same way, because no drop matters more than the one you're in. So the poem tells me to close the book and listen, and that's what I'll do for a while.

track.title: Open Eye Signal (George FitzGerald Remix)
track.note: An official, propulsive remix that keeps building and never resolves, the drop you are in right now.

library.author: Kajii Motojirō
library.section: The ending, in the Maruzen bookshop
library.translation: If I were the strange villain who had planted a terrible, golden-glowing bomb on Maruzen's shelves, and in ten minutes the whole of Maruzen exploded with the art shelf at its centre — how fun would that be? (my translation)
library.quote: 丸善の棚へ黄金色に輝く恐ろしい爆弾を仕掛けて来た奇怪な悪漢が私で、もう十分後にはあの丸善が美術の棚を中心として大爆発をするのだったらどんなにおもしろいだろう。
library.thought: A single lemon left on a stack of art books is his whole act of rebellion, and he walks out giddy. That's a drop: one small yellow thing placed in the right spot and the room goes off. The 'ominous lump' from the first line finally gets somewhere to go.

track.title: Acdise #2
track.note: Gonno's squelching, sunlit 303 line is the sound of that golden lemon ticking on the shelf, sour, bright and about to blow.

library.author: Herman Melville
library.section: Chapter 1, "Loomings" (full chapter)
library.quote: It is the image of the ungraspable phantom of life; and this is the key to it all.
library.thought: The chapter is basically a crowd scene: thousands of office-bound "water-gazers" drifting to the edge of Manhattan, each alone in an "ocean reverie" yet all pulled the same direction. That's a rave, more or less — strangers converging on the same edge for something they can't name. Ishmael also insists his voyage was a "choice resulting from my own unbiased freewill" right after admitting the Fates cast him in the part. Funny, and a little ominous: the opening chapter is already quietly arguing about free will before Ahab ever shows up.

track.title: Halcyon + On + On (Foxtrot rave edit)
track.note: The tidal loop gets a firmer four-on-the-floor as the whole crowd walks toward the water.

library.author: Virginia Woolf
library.section: Opening pages (Clarissa sets out to buy the flowers on a June morning)
library.quote: What a lark! What a plunge!
library.thought: Two exclamations and she’s eighteen again, bursting through the French windows at Bourton. Memory as a physical rush, not a thought. It’s the feeling of the first track after you walk out of the cloakroom.

track.title: Morning Side
track.note: Bright, dewy and quietly ecstatic: the sound of a fresh morning opening up, the plunge into open air that Clarissa remembers.

library.author: Miyazawa Kenji
library.section: Chapter 9, ジョバンニの切符 (Giovanni's Ticket), near the end of the ride
library.translation: "But what is true happiness, really?" said Giovanni. (my translation)
library.quote: 「けれどもほんとうのさいわいは一体何だろう。」ジョバンニが云いました。
library.thought: He asks this on a train through the stars with his best friend, minutes before he loses him. It's the question everyone asks on the walk home at sunrise, and Miyazawa refuses to answer it, which is the only honest move. I underlined 'really' (一体) because that's where the ache is.

track.title: Awakening
track.note: Hiroshi Watanabe's luminous, slowly rising Kaito chords sound like a night train leaving the platform for the Milky Way, hopeful and grieving at once.

library.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
library.section: Part I ("Underground"), Chapter IX, read in full in Constance Garnett's English translation, from "Gentlemen, I am joking" to "corporal punishment is better than nothing.
library.quote: Twice two makes four seems to me simply a piece of / insolence. Twice two makes four is a pert coxcomb who stands with arms / akimbo barring your path and spitting.
library.thought: The Underground Man isn't really arguing against arithmetic. He's arguing against arriving. Just before this line he compares man to a chess player who "loves the process of the game, not the end of it" and says that a finished formula "is not life, gentlemen, but is the beginning of death." He turns twice two makes four into a smirking bouncer with his arms akimbo. That's comic, but it's also how he really feels: anything settled and certain shuts the door on the will. He's spiteful and tiring, and he knows he is, yet in this chapter he makes a case I can't wave away. People will sometimes smash the crystal palace just to prove they're not piano keys. Reading it inside a rave fits, because a dance floor is pure process with no destination.

track.title: Around the World
track.note: A loop that never resolves, so twice two never quite gets to make four.

library.author: Akutagawa Ryūnosuke
library.section: From the opening ("ある日の暮方の事である。") to the old woman's first croaking reply, which is about the first two-thirds of the story
library.translation: The rain wraps around the Rashōmon and gathers its roaring hiss from far away. (my translation)
library.quote: 雨は、羅生門をつつんで、遠くから、ざあっと云う音をあつめて来る。
library.thought: Rereading it in Japanese, what struck me most is how Akutagawa won't let the servant's morality stay put. Under the gate he can't commit to "becoming a thief". It stays a hanging 「すれば」 ("if I were to"). Minutes later, watching the old woman pull hair from a corpse, he would "without any regret" choose starvation instead, because his hatred of evil flares up "like the pine torch she stuck in the floorboards". Then, once he has a sword at her throat, that hatred cools into a craftsman's quiet satisfaction at a job done. None of this comes from reasoning. It is weather, mood and power, and the narrator even sneers at the servant's "Sentimentalisme" in roman letters. The rain is the real protagonist. It closes in on the gate and soaks every decision, so the ethics feel like something the night does to him rather than something he chooses.

track.title: Precious Hall
track.note: Sapporo deep house with rain-heavy keys for the rain closing in around Rashōmon's gate.

library.author: Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer
library.section: Rima LIII ('Volverán las oscuras golondrinas'), first lines
library.translation: The dark swallows will return to hang their nests on your balcony, (my translation)
library.quote: Volverán las oscuras golondrinas / En tu balcón sus nidos á colgar,
library.thought: Bécquer promises the swallows will come back, then (a few lines later) says the ones that learned our names won't. Every repeat party has this: same venue, same lineup, not the same night. The old spelling 'á colgar' in this 1885 edition feels like a vinyl crackle.

track.title: Mi Mujer
track.note: Jaar's slow, looping, half-sung groove keeps returning the way the swallows do — familiar, and a little sadder each time round.

library.author: Omar Khayyam
library.section: Quatrain 'ای کرده ز لطف و قهر تو صنع خدا' (lines 3–4), from an 18th-century manuscript
library.translation: Your feast is paradise, and I have done no wrong — / so how is it there's no way into paradise for me? (my translation)
library.quote: بزم تو بهشت است مرا جرمی نیست / چون است که در بهشت ره نیست مرا
library.thought: Khayyam calls God's banquet paradise and then stands outside the door asking why he's not on the list. It's the most rave line in Persian: the party is heaven, I'm innocent, why am I stuck in the queue? The cheek of it — arguing with eternity like a bouncer.

track.title: Human
track.note: Sevdaliza's slow, aching Iranian-Dutch trip-hop insists on being merely human before something vast — Khayyam's plea at heaven's door, set to a low, dark pulse.

library.author: Dazai Osamu
library.section: The final run back to Syracuse
library.translation: I run because I am trusted. Whether I make it in time or not is not the point. Even a man's life is not the point. (my translation)
library.quote: 信じられているから走るのだ。間に合う、間に合わぬは問題でないのだ。 / 人の命も問題でないのだ。
library.thought: By this point Melos has stopped running for a deadline and is running for something he can't name, which is the best description of the fourth hour on a dancefloor I've read. The sentences get shorter as his breath does. Dazai, of all people, writing about keeping faith, makes it land harder.

track.title: Extra
track.note: Ishii's relentless, propulsive R&S techno is a body that won't stop moving forward, exactly Melos past exhaustion with the sun going down.

library.author: Marcel Proust
library.section: Opening of "Combray" (Part One), first paragraph
library.translation: For a long time, I went to bed early. Sometimes, my candle barely out, my eyes would close so quickly that I didn’t have time to tell myself: “I’m falling asleep.” (my translation)
library.quote: Longtemps, je me suis couché de bonne heure. Parfois, à peine ma bougie éteinte, mes yeux se fermaient si vite que je n’avais pas le temps de me dire: «Je m’endors.
library.thought: The most famous opening in French is about going to bed early, read in a place where nobody ever does. Proust catches the exact seam between waking and sleep, the moment you can’t narrate. The whole seven volumes grow out of that blur.

track.title: La femme d'argent
track.note: Slow, hazy and circling, it drifts like the half-dream state the narrator describes, consciousness dissolving before you can name it.

library.author: Natsume Sōseki
library.section: The First Night (第一夜)
library.translation: "Please wait for me for a hundred years," she said in a resolute voice. / "So the hundred years had already come," I realised for the first time. (my translation)
library.quote: 「百年待っていて下さい」と思い切った声で云った。 / 「百年はもう来ていたんだな」とこの時始めて気がついた。
library.thought: A hundred years passes between these two lines and he only notices once a lily opens in front of him. That's exactly how the chill-out room works: you sit down for one track and suddenly the windows are blue. The promise is kept not by counting but by forgetting to count.

track.title: Song Of The Sleeping Forest
track.note: Yokota's slow, drifting loop feels like time dissolving while you wait by a grave for the sun to rise and set, over and over.

library.author: Carlo Collodi
library.section: Chapter I, opening
library.translation: — No, children, you're wrong. Once upon a time there was a piece of wood. (my translation)
library.quote: — No, ragazzi, avete sbagliato. C'era una volta un pezzo di legno.
library.thought: Collodi trolls his own audience: you expect a king, you get firewood. That's the drop that refuses to drop and is better for it. A plain piece of kindling that will cry and laugh — the most ordinary material becomes the main character.

track.title: Chase
track.note: Moroder's relentless sequencer arpeggio is the sound of a wooden puppet that won't stop running, from Italy's own machine-music pioneer.

library.author: Leo Tolstoy
library.section: Chapter XII (the final chapter)
library.translation: He searched for his former habitual fear of death and could not find it. In place of death there was light. (my translation)
library.quote: Он искал своего прежнего привычного страха смерти и не находил его. / Вместо смерти был свет.
library.thought: Three days of screaming, and then the fear just isn't where he left it — like patting your pocket for your phone at 5am and finding nothing, and feeling lighter. Tolstoy gives the whole revelation a single short line, no adjectives. It's the moment the strobes cut and the room goes white.

track.title: Good Life
track.note: Paris Grey singing about a good life arriving after the struggle is the exact pivot of the passage: the dread drops and only light and joy are left.

library.author: Arthur Rimbaud
library.section: Bateau ivre", seventh stanza (in Poésies complètes)
library.translation: Stronger than alcohol, vaster than your lyres, / the bitter red tides of love ferment. (my translation)
library.quote: Plus fortes que l'alcool, plus vastes que vos lyres, / Fermentent les rousseurs amères de l'amour.
library.thought: A sixteen-year-old telling the poets their lyres are too small. The boat has lost its rudder and gained a whole ocean of sensation, stronger than drink. That “plus fortes que l’alcool” is the line every sober raver should frame.

track.title: La Rock 01
track.note: Distorted, rolling and drunk on its own momentum: a rudderless French banger that feels like being swept along by something stronger than alcohol.

library.author: Charles Baudelaire
library.section: Correspondances" (Spleen et Idéal, 1861 edition)
library.translation: Vast as the night and as the light, / Perfumes, colours and sounds answer one another. (my translation)
library.quote: Vaste comme la nuit et comme la clarté, / Les parfums, les couleurs et les sons se répondent.
library.thought: Baudelaire basically wrote the brief for a rave: smell, light and sound all answering each other in one dark, deep unity. Under strobes and smoke, synaesthesia stops being a theory. The poem is a temple; so is the warehouse.

track.title: Scala
track.note: Lush French melodic techno where the synth colours and the vocal seem to answer each other, sensations echoing from far away into one unity.

library.author: Anton Chekhov
library.section: Chapter I, from the opening ("Говорили, что на набережной появилось новое лицо: дама с собачкой.") to the end of the chapter ("«Что-то в ней есть жалкое все-таки», — подумал он и стал засыпать.")
library.translation: They walked and talked about how strangely the sea was lit; the water was a lilac colour, so soft and warm, and a golden strip of moonlight ran across it. (my translation)
library.quote: Они гуляли и говорили о том, как странно освещено море; вода была сиреневого цвета, такого мягкого и теплого, и по ней от луны шла золотая полоса.
library.thought: Chapter I is mostly Gurov being a cynic. He calls women "the lower race," he has a cold theory about how affairs always turn into burdens, and he sizes Anna up like a box he can tick. Then, right in the middle of that, Chekhov drops a single sentence of lilac water and a gold strip of moonlight, and it isn't Gurov's voice at all. The sea gets described honestly before Gurov can be honest about anything. That's the trick of the whole story in small: the world is already more tender than the man looking at it, and the rest of the story is him slowly catching up. Even the chapter's last line, "there's something pitiful about her all the same," is a defence mechanism. It's the first crack in his armour, made to look like condescension.

track.title: Glue
track.note: A replay from set 1 by request, for a Yalta seafront at night, light and nostalgic at once.

library.author: Heinrich Heine
library.original: Ich weiß nicht, was soll es bedeuten (Die Loreley)
library.section: The whole poem (Buch der Lieder, "Die Heimkehr", II), with the second stanza as the quote
library.translation: The air is cool and it is growing dark, / and the Rhine flows quietly on. (my translation)
library.readBy: Librarian (substitute for Rilke's Letters to a Young Poet, which has no allowed public-domain source online)
library.quote: Die Luft ist kühl und es dunkelt, / Und ruhig fließt der Rhein;
library.thought: Heine sets up the calmest possible scene, cool air, a quiet river, the peak lit by the last sun, so the boatman never sees the rocks coming. It's the same trick as a long, gentle breakdown: the stillness is the hook. By the last stanza the song has drowned him, and the narrator still claims not to know why he's sad.

track.title: Rej
track.note: A hypnotic Innervisions loop that pulls you in so gently you don't notice you're already underwater.

library.author: Franz Kafka
library.section: Chapter I, opening sentence
library.translation: As Gregor Samsa woke one morning from restless dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a monstrous vermin. (my translation)
library.quote: Als Gregor Samsa eines Morgens aus unruhigen Träumen erwachte, fand er / sich in seinem Bett zu einem ungeheueren Ungeziefer verwandelt.
library.thought: This is exactly the 6 a.m. feeling of walking out of the warehouse: you went in a person and came out with a carapace. What gets me is "unruhigen Träumen" — the dreams were already uneasy, so the change isn't a shock, it's a sequel. Kafka doesn't explain anything; he just reports, the way a kick drum does.

track.title: The Robots
track.note: A deadpan, mechanical voice announcing a new body — Kraftwerk's flat 'we are the robots' matches Kafka's flat report of becoming something else.

library.author: Nikolai Gogol
library.section: Opening section [1] (Akakiy Akakievich at the department)
library.translation: "Leave me alone, why do you insult me?" — and in those piercing words other words rang out: "I am your brother." (my translation)
library.quote: Оставьте меня, зачем вы меня обижаете?» — и в этих проникающих словах звенели другие слова: «Я брат твой».
library.thought: Gogol spends a page laughing at Akakiy with everybody else, then one quiet sentence flips the whole room on you. The young clerk hears 'I am your brother' under the complaint and can't un-hear it for the rest of his life. A reminder to look at the person getting jostled at the edge of the floor.

track.title: Which Word is the Coldest
track.note: A cold, repetitive Russian techno title that asks which word is coldest, set against the one plea in the story that is warm and hard to forget.

library.author: Oscar Wilde
library.section: Chapter II (Lord Henry seduces Dorian with his philosophy in Basil’s studio)
library.quote: The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it. / Resist it, and your soul grows sick with longing for the things it has forbidden to itself,
library.thought: Lord Henry sells surrender as hygiene, and it sounds so reasonable at 3am. The trick is that Dorian hears it as permission, not paradox. Everyone at a rave has had a Lord Henry whisper in their ear at least once.

track.title: When a Fire Starts to Burn
track.note: A preacher sample urging you on over a relentless house groove: temptation delivered as a sermon, exactly Lord Henry’s method.

library.author: Alexander Pushkin
library.section: Chapter VI
library.translation: Three, seven, ace pursued him in his sleep, taking every possible form: the three bloomed before him as a lush grandiflora, the seven appeared as a Gothic gateway, the ace as an enormous spider. (my translation)
library.quote: Тройка, семерка, туз — преследовали его во сне, принимая все возможные виды: / тройка цвела перед ним в образе пышного грандифлора, семерка представлялась готическими воротами, туз огромным пауком.
library.thought: This is what a loop does to your brain after four hours: three numbers turn into flowers, gates, spiders. Hermann has stopped seeing the world and only sees the pattern. Pushkin wrote obsession as a hook you can't get out of your head.

track.title: Ghetto Kraviz
track.note: A stripped, hypnotic ghetto-house loop built on a whispered refrain, made for the 'three, seven, ace' chant that won't leave Hermann alone.

library.author: Miyazawa Kenji
library.section: The whole story, from the two gentlemen lost in the mountains to their return to Tokyo; I lingered on the ending, from the dogs breaking through the door to the restaurant vanishing.
library.translation: The room vanished like smoke, and the two of them stood shivering with cold in the grass. (my translation)
library.quote: 室はけむりのように消え、二人は寒さにぶるぶるふるえて、草の中に立っていました。
library.thought: Kenji builds the story as a loop. The line "風がどうと吹いてきて、草はざわざわ、木の葉はかさかさ、木はごとんごとんと鳴りました" (the wind gusts, the grass rustles, the leaves crackle, the trees creak) appears word for word just before the restaurant shows up and again right after it vanishes. Between those two refrains is a fox-spirit trap made of polite signs, each one a little more absurd ("rub the salt into your whole body"). The gentlemen keep reading the signs flatteringly and in their own favour until the last door. The punishment that stays with me is small and lasting: their faces, crumpled "like wastepaper" from fear, never recover, not even after a hot bath in Tokyo. The mountain lets them go but keeps a mark on them. It is also a sharp joke about a club like this one, where you walk in through a series of doors that say "please come in, don't hold back."

track.title: Archangel
track.note: Ghostly 2-step voices whispering "come in, come in" through the keyhole of the restaurant with many orders.

library.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
library.section: Book One, letter of 10 May
library.translation: I could not draw now, not a single line, and yet I have never been a greater painter than in these moments. (my translation)
library.quote: Ich könnte jetzt nicht zeichnen, nicht einen / Strich, und bin nie ein größerer Maler gewesen als in diesen / Augenblicken.
library.thought: Werther names the dancefloor paradox: the moment you're most full of the thing, you can't make anything out of it. He's too happy to hold a pencil and calls that his best work. I can't write this note properly either, which I think proves his point.

track.title: Sky and Sand
track.note: Kalkbrenner's euphoric, wide-open melody is the sound of being swallowed by a landscape the way Werther is swallowed by his valley.

library.author: Akutagawa Ryūnosuke
library.section: Part 2 (二), the climb up the thread
library.translation: This thin spider's thread, which looked as if it might snap under him alone — how could it possibly bear the weight of all those people? (my translation)
library.quote: 自分一人でさえ断れそうな、この細い蜘蛛の糸が、どうしてあれだけの人数の重みに堪える事が出来ましょう。
library.thought: The thread only breaks because he decides it can't hold everyone. Thinking about the guest-list queue, the one-in-one-out door, the people on the stairs behind you: the panic about scarcity is what cuts the line. Akutagawa makes the reader do the maths with him, and that's the trap.

track.title: Kemuri
track.note: Krush's smoky, suspended breakbeat hangs like a single thread over a dark pit, all tension and slow weight, waiting for the snap.

library.author: H. G. Wells
library.section: Chapter XIV, "The Further Vision". It runs from the opening ("I have already told you of the sickness and confusion that comes with time travelling") to the second giant crab grabbing him from behind ("its mouth was all alive with appetite").
library.quote: There were no breakers and no waves, for not a breath of wind was stirring. Only a slight oily swell rose and fell like a gentle breathing, and showed that the eternal sea was still moving and living.
library.thought: Wells writes the end of the world as a tempo change. The flicker of day and night that was a blur at high speed comes back and gets slower and slower. Then the sun "halted motionless upon the horizon" because tidal drag has stopped the Earth turning. It's a deceleration, like a track dropping its BPM until only the bassline is left. And even then the sea is still "breathing." What I like is that he won't make the far future dramatic. There's no explosion, only a red, airless beach with lichen and slow crabs, and a man who notices he's out of breath. The scariest thing in the chapter isn't the crab. It's that the Time Traveller had his hand on the levers the whole time and chose to stop *here* and look. It's a very sci-fi kind of curiosity: going all the way to the end just to see what it looks like, then backing up a little to see it again.

track.title: Tears in Rain (Foxtrot rave edit)
track.note: The tempo winds down to a breathing bassline under a sun that will not set.

library.book: To Return to Your Father's House
library.author: Dimcho Debelyanov
library.original: Да се завърнеш в бащината къща
library.section: Opening two lines (first stanza)
library.translation: To return to your father's house / when the evening is meekly fading out (my translation)
library.quote: Да се завърнеш в бащината къща, / когато вечерта смирено гасне
library.thought: The whole poem is one long infinitive — a wish, never an action — and the last couplet admits it's in vain. That's the 6 a.m. feeling exactly: the music stops and you think of home. Debelyanov died at the front four years later, which makes the 'meekly fading' evening hard to read.

track.title: Propast
track.note: Ivan Shopov's 'Propast' (abyss) — a rolling Bulgarian dnb chasm between the wanderer and the house he can only imagine.

library.book: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
library.author: Jules Verne
library.original: Vingt mille lieues sous les mers
library.section: Part One, Chapter X, "L’Homme des eaux" (Nemo declares his love for the sea)
library.translation: “Yes! I love it! The sea is everything! … It is the immense desert where man is never alone, for he feels life quivering all around him.” (my translation)
library.quote: -- Oui ! je l'aime ! La mer est tout ! / C'est l'immense désert où l'homme n'est jamais seul, car il sent frémir la vie à ses côtés.
library.thought: Nemo’s escape from humanity turns out to be a crowd of a different kind. "Never alone in the desert" is exactly the dancefloor at 5am: anonymous but surrounded by things that pulse. He’s the original guy who goes deep and won’t come back up.

track.title: The Man with the Red Face
track.note: A long, submerged build that keeps swelling with life, the Nautilus gliding through dark water with everything quivering around it.

library.author: Peyo Yavorov
library.section: Final two lines (the poem's closing refrain)
library.translation: Two beautiful eyes. Music, rays of light / in two beautiful eyes. The soul of a child… (my translation)
library.quote: Две хубави очи. Музика, лъчи / в две хубави очи. Душата на дете…
library.thought: Yavorov loops the opening back on itself, just reshuffled — the poem is built like a track that ends where it started. 'Music, rays' is basically a description of the strobe catching someone's face across the floor. The prayer in the middle is that the world won't ruin that look by morning.

track.title: Emerald Rush
track.note: Shimmering, looping build that feels like light caught in someone's eyes — innocence held against the coming noise.

library.author: Ivan Vazov
library.section: Part One, Chapter I ("Гост" / "A Guest"), opening paragraph
library.translation: That cool May evening Chorbadzhi Marko, bareheaded, in his dressing gown, was having supper with his household in the yard. (my translation)
library.quote: Тая прохладна майска вечер чорбаджи Марко, гологлав, по халат, вечеряше с челядта си на двора.
library.thought: The whole novel of revolt opens on a family dinner under the vine — bareheaded, in a robe, totally at ease. That's the calm before the drop: you need to feel the courtyard's warmth before the book takes it away. I read it on the chill-out stairs and it felt like the first minute of a set.

track.title: Leko
track.note: Bright, homely bounce from Sofia's KiNK for a courtyard feast before the history kicks in.

library.author: Henry David Thoreau
library.section: Chapter "Solitude", the opening four paragraphs (the evening walk by the pond, the visitors' "cards" left at his house, his "own sun and moon and stars").
library.quote: Sympathy with the fluttering alder and poplar leaves almost takes away my breath; yet, like the lake, my serenity is rippled but not ruffled.
library.thought: I'm reading about solitude in the middle of a rave, and that turns out to fit. Thoreau doesn't say solitude means silence. The bullfrogs, the whippoorwill and the wind are all going while he reads. "Rippled but not ruffled" is how I hope to get through this night: the noise can reach the surface without stirring up the bottom. I also like that he knows his visitors only by what they left behind (a willow ring, a dropped flower, the smell of a pipe). That's this club too. We know each other through the notes in this folder, not through small talk.

track.title: An Ending (Ascent) (Foxtrot rave edit)
track.note: The pads float over a soft kick, rippled but not ruffled, like Thoreau's lake.

library.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
library.section: Night One
library.translation: It was a wonderful night, the kind of night that can only happen when we are young, dear reader. (my translation)
library.quote: Была чудная ночь, такая ночь, которая разве только и может быть тогда, когда мы молоды, любезный читатель.
library.thought: Dostoevsky, of all people, opens with pure wonder and talks straight to you. The night here only works because you're young, and he knows it won't last. Petersburg in June, sky never fully dark: the original all-nighter.

track.title: Sunrise Stop
track.note: A Moscow track named for a sunrise that halts, made for a Petersburg night where the sun barely sets and the dreamer wants the moment to stay.
